reponse:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dedicated Activation Ranges for Camera and Register Tokens in VGGT
PROPOSAL: Quantize the 1.2-billion-parameter VGGT aggregator to 8-bit weights and 8-bit activations, giving the camera token and the register tokens their own activation range in every block while image tokens keep per-channel ranges fitted on 64 calibration sequences from CO3Dv2. Evaluate relative rotation and translation accuracy (thresholds of 5 and 30 degrees, plus the area under the curve) on held-out RealEstate10K scenes, and point map error on 7-Scenes, and log the share of clipped activation values per block.
CONTROLS: Compare against a single shared activation range for all tokens, against per-tensor and per-channel static ranges, and against the full-precision model. Repeat the calibration with five seeds of sequence selection and report the spread of every metric.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Dedicated ranges should recover most of the pose accuracy lost by a shared range, with the largest gain in the early blocks where special tokens dominate the extremes. The idea fails if the gap stays inside the seed-to-seed spread or if clipped-value shares do not drop.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Coverage-Driven Selection of Calibration Sequences for Multi-View Quantization
PROPOSAL: The plan draws a small calibration set by embedding every candidate sequence from CO3Dv2, ScanNet and a driving corpus with the pretrained vision backbone, clustering the embeddings into thirty-two groups and taking the sequence nearest each centre, so that the set covers the main modes of the data and skips rare outliers. VGGT is then quantized to 8-bit weights and 6-bit activations with ranges fitted on that set, and camera pose and point map accuracy are measured on held-out scenes from each source. The study repeats the draw twenty times to record how much the final accuracy moves with the choice of sequences.
CONTROLS: The coverage-driven set is compared in prose terms with a uniformly random draw of the same size, with a draw confined to a single source, and with a draw built only from the sequences whose activations have the largest ranges, and the full-precision model gives the reference accuracy. Every draw uses the same quantizer and the same number of sequences.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Coverage-driven sets should give a higher mean pose accuracy and a clearly smaller spread across draws than random sets, especially on the source that the single-source draw leaves out. If the spread of the coverage-driven draws matches that of random draws, the idea has failed.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Offline Rotation Smoothing of Heavy-Tailed Tokens Before Quantisation
PROPOSAL: Apply an orthogonal Hadamard rotation to the input of each attention and feed-forward projection in VGGT, folding the inverse rotation into the neighbouring weights offline so that the network is unchanged in full precision and no extra operation runs at test time. The rotation spreads the extreme channel values of the camera and register tokens over many channels, and the model is then quantised to 4-bit weights and 6-bit activations with ranges fitted on 32 sequences. We analyse kurtosis of the activations per layer before and after rotation, and we judge the result by pose and point map accuracy on RealEstate10K and 7-Scenes.
CONTROLS: Compare the rotated model with the unrotated one under the same quantisation, with a per-channel scaling approach borrowed from language models, and with a learnable clipping scheme, keeping the calibration sequences identical. Add a run that rotates only the image tokens to localise where the gain comes from, and repeat with three seeds of the random sign pattern.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: The rotation should lower activation kurtosis markedly and recover much of the accuracy lost at 4-bit weights, with the smallest recovery in the final depth head. It could fail if the special tokens keep their extreme values after rotation, which would show up as unchanged kurtosis.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Post-Training Quantization of the Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer
PROPOSAL: Study post-training quantization (PTQ) of the Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer (VGGT) by converting its weights to 4-bit integers and its activations to 8-bit integers, with quantization ranges set from a small calibration set of 48 sequences. Quality is measured with absolute trajectory error (ATE) on indoor handheld sequences from the Technical University of Munich benchmark, with the area under the curve (AUC) of relative pose accuracy on RealEstate10K, and with point map error on 7-Scenes. Peak memory and frames per second are recorded for the full-precision and quantized models on the same machine, so that savings are measured rather than assumed.
CONTROLS: Compare against the full-precision model, against rounding to the nearest integer with min-max ranges, and against a second-order weight rounding method applied to weights only. Hold the calibration sequences fixed and repeat the selection with four different seeds to check stability.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: Weight-only 4-bit rounding should stay close to full precision on pose accuracy, while 8-bit activations should add a visible drop on scenes with large depth ranges. The plan fails if the quantized model loses more than a few points of accuracy or shows no measurable memory saving.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Measuring Real Memory and Speed Gains of an Integer VGGT
PROPOSAL: Export the 4-bit weight and 8-bit activation version of VGGT into packed integer matrix-multiplication routines written with open-source tools and run it on one consumer graphics card and one data-centre accelerator. Sequences of 8, 16 and 32 frames from CO3Dv2 are processed with batch size one, and we record peak memory, frames per second and the time spent in attention, in the feed-forward layers and in the prediction heads. Accuracy is checked in the same runs by relative rotation and translation accuracy on held-out scenes.
CONTROLS: Compare with the full-precision model and with the half-precision model on identical sequences, include a simulated quantiser that keeps weights in floating point to separate rounding effects from kernel effects, and repeat each timing twenty times after a warm-up to report medians and spread.
COST: 250
PREDICTION: Packed integer kernels should cut weight memory by roughly three quarters and give a visible speed-up for long sequences, less so for short ones. If the measured speed-up is below ten percent or accuracy drifts from the simulated run, the approach has failed.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Layer Sensitivity Map for Mixed-Precision Quantization of VGGT
PROPOSAL: Measure how much each block of VGGT suffers when only that block is quantized to 4-bit weights and 6-bit activations, using 32 calibration sequences from CO3Dv2 and held-out scenes from ScanNet and 7-Scenes. The sensitivity ranking then drives a mixed-precision assignment that keeps the most fragile blocks and the camera head at 8 bits and pushes the rest to 4 bits, under a fixed average bit-width of 5.
CONTROLS: Compare the sensitivity-driven assignment with a uniform assignment at the same average bit-width, with an assignment that keeps the first and last blocks at higher precision, and with a random assignment repeated over five seeds. The full-precision model supplies the reference accuracy.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: The sensitivity-driven assignment should keep pose and point map accuracy close to full precision and clearly above the uniform and random assignments. The study fails if the ranking changes sharply between calibration draws, since the assignment would then not be reliable.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: How Many Calibration Sequences Does VGGT Quantization Need
PROPOSAL: We study the size of the calibration set by quantizing VGGT to 8-bit weights and 8-bit activations with ranges fitted on 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 and 128 sequences drawn from CO3Dv2 and ScanNet. For each size we draw fifteen independent sets, measure camera pose accuracy and point map error on held-out RealEstate10K and 7-Scenes scenes, and report the mean and the spread across draws. We also record how often the fitted range of the camera token changes by more than ten percent between draws.
CONTROLS: We compare against the full-precision model, against ranges taken from the maximum value of a single sequence, and against ranges taken from a percentile of all activations in the largest set. We keep the quantizer, the evaluation scenes and the frame count per sequence fixed across all sizes.
COST: 70
PREDICTION: We expect accuracy to saturate near 32 sequences and the spread across draws to shrink steadily until then. We would consider the premise wrong if even 128 sequences leave a spread comparable to that of 8 sequences.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Calibrating on Indoor Scenes and Testing on Outdoor Scenes
PROPOSAL: Fit the quantization ranges of an 8-bit VGGT on 40 indoor sequences from ScanNet and test generalization on three kinds of unseen scenes: further indoor rooms, object-centric captures from CO3Dv2, and outdoor trajectories from the KITTI odometry benchmark. Report relative pose accuracy, absolute trajectory error and point map error for each, and compare with ranges fitted on a mixed set of equal size that contains all three kinds. The gap between the two calibration choices measures how far the ranges transfer.
CONTROLS: Compare against the full-precision model, against a dynamic scheme that recomputes ranges per input sequence, and against ranges fitted on the evaluation scenes themselves as a reference for what is attainable. Repeat the indoor draw with five seeds.
COST: 220
PREDICTION: Ranges fitted indoors should transfer well to indoor rooms and object captures but lose noticeably on outdoor trajectories with large depth ranges. If outdoor accuracy under indoor ranges matches the mixed set, the concern about distribution shift is unfounded.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Clipping Percentiles for Special-Token Activations in Low-Bit VGGT
PROPOSAL: Heavy-tailed activations of the camera token and the register tokens occupy most of the quantization range, so this plan tests percentile clipping applied only to those tokens. VGGT is quantized to 4-bit weights and 6-bit activations, the clipping percentile for special tokens is varied between 99.0 and 99.99, and ranges for image tokens stay at their maximum value. Pose accuracy and point map error are evaluated on held-out RealEstate10K and 7-Scenes scenes, using ranges fitted on 32 calibration sequences.
CONTROLS: Compare against clipping applied to all tokens at the same percentile, against no clipping at all, and against a clipping value learned by gradient descent on the output error of each block. Repeat each configuration with four seeds of sequence selection.
COST: 140
PREDICTION: A percentile near 99.9 for special tokens should give the best trade-off, recovering most of the accuracy lost without clipping and beating all-token clipping on pose accuracy. The approach fails if accuracy is insensitive to the percentile, which would show that the tails are not the cause of the loss.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Head-by-Head Quantization of Depth, Point and Camera Outputs
PROPOSAL: Quantize the backbone of VGGT to 4-bit weights and 8-bit activations, then give each prediction head (depth, point map, camera pose and tracking) its own precision, from 4-bit up to full precision, using 32 calibration sequences from CO3Dv2. Evaluate depth error on ScanNet, point map error on 7-Scenes and pose accuracy on RealEstate10K to find which heads tolerate low precision and which need more.
CONTROLS: Compare each head setting with the backbone-only result, with the full-precision model, and with a uniform 4-bit model across all heads. Repeat the calibration with three seeds and report the spread of each metric.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: The camera head should be the most sensitive to low precision and the depth head the most tolerant, so a mixed assignment should beat uniform 4-bit. The plan fails if all heads degrade by similar amounts, since a per-head choice would then offer no advantage.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dedicated Ranges for Camera and Register Tokens in Low-Bit VGGT
PROPOSAL: Quantize the VGGT aggregator to 4-bit weights and 8-bit activations, giving the camera token and the register tokens a dedicated activation range in every block while image tokens keep per-channel ranges fitted on 32 calibration sequences from CO3Dv2. Evaluate relative rotation and translation accuracy on held-out RealEstate10K scenes and point map error on 7-Scenes, and record the share of clipped activation values per block.
CONTROLS: Compare the dedicated-range scheme with a single shared range for all tokens, with the full-precision reference, and with a channel-scaling method adapted from language models, using the same calibration sequences and the same bit-widths held fixed. Repeat every setting with five seeds of sequence selection and report the spread.
COST: 180
PREDICTION: Dedicated ranges should recover most of the pose accuracy lost by the shared range, mostly in early blocks. The claim is refuted if the gap stays inside the spread across seeds.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dedicated Ranges for Patch Embedding Features in Low-Bit VGGT
PROPOSAL: Quantize the pretrained image backbone inside VGGT to 4-bit weights and 8-bit activations, giving the patch embedding and the first transformer blocks a dedicated activation range while later blocks keep per-channel ranges fitted on 32 calibration images from ImageNet. Evaluate top-1 accuracy of the backbone on the ImageNet validation split and cosine similarity of its output features, and record the share of clipped activation values per block.
CONTROLS: Compare the dedicated-range scheme with a single shared range for the 2D classifier backbone, with the full-precision reference of a smaller depth-only network, and with a channel-scaling method evaluated on a text benchmark, using the same calibration images and the same bit-widths held fixed. Repeat every setting with five seeds of image selection and report the spread.
COST: 180
PREDICTION: Dedicated ranges should recover most of the classification accuracy lost by the shared range, mostly in early blocks. The claim is refuted if the gap stays inside the spread across seeds.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Stability of Quantization Ranges Across Calibration Draws in VGGT
PROPOSAL: Fit 8-bit activation ranges for VGGT on sets of 16 sequences chosen by clustering backbone embeddings of CO3Dv2, ScanNet and a driving corpus, and draw twelve independent sets. For each draw, measure camera pose accuracy and point map error on held-out scenes, and track how far the fitted range of every block moves from draw to draw. A summary statistic of this movement gives the stability of the procedure.
CONTROLS: Vary the draw of sequences while holding the quantizer and the frame order fixed; vary the source dataset of the draw; compare against uniformly random draws of the same count; and use the full-precision model as reference. Evaluate every setting on the same held-out scenes.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: Range movement across draws should be small relative to the range itself, and pose accuracy should vary by only a small amount. Instability shows as a spread larger than the gain over random draws.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Order and Initialisation Effects in VGGT Activation Quantization
PROPOSAL: Quantize VGGT to 8-bit activations with ranges fitted on a fixed set of 16 sequences taken from CO3Dv2 and ScanNet, then perturb the procedure twelve times by reordering frames inside each sequence and restarting the rounding parameters from random initial values. For each run, measure camera pose accuracy and point map error on held-out scenes, and track how far the fitted range of every block moves from run to run.
CONTROLS: Vary the frame order inside each sequence while holding the set of sequences and the quantizer fixed; vary the starting values of the rounding parameters; compare against a reversed frame order of the same count; and use the full-precision model as reference. Evaluate every setting on the same held-out scenes.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: Range movement across runs should be small relative to the range itself, and pose accuracy should vary by only a small amount. Instability shows as a spread larger than the gain over reversed orders.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Where Heavy Tails Break Quantization in VGGT: Low-Bit Activation Study
PROPOSAL: Quantize all linear layers of VGGT to weight and activation bit-widths of 4, 6 and 8, using static ranges fitted on 32 calibration sequences from CO3Dv2. Evaluate pose accuracy on RealEstate10K, point map error on 7-Scenes, and the fraction of activation values that fall in the top percentile of the range, per block, so that the point where special-token extremes begin to dominate becomes visible.
CONTROLS: Compare each low-bit model with the full-precision reference, with a version that keeps special-token activations in 16-bit, and with a version that quantizes only the weights, holding the calibration sequences and the evaluation scenes fixed. Repeat the three bit-width settings with four seeds of sequence selection.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: Accuracy should fall sharply at the lowest activation bit-width and the 16-bit special-token version should recover most of it. If every bit-width stays within the seed spread of the reference, the concern about heavy tails does not arise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Where Rounding Matters for Weights in VGGT: Mild-Precision Study
PROPOSAL: Convert every projection matrix of VGGT to weight precisions of 8, 12 and 16 while activations remain in 16-bit, with static ranges estimated from 32 calibration sequences drawn out of CO3Dv2. Report pose accuracy on RealEstate10K, point map error on 7-Scenes, and the mean absolute rounding error of the weights, block by block, to locate where weight rounding starts to matter.
CONTROLS: Set each mild-precision model against the full-precision reference, against a version that leaves the camera head in 32-bit, and against a version that quantizes only the activations, holding the calibration sequences and the evaluation scenes fixed. Repeat the three precision settings with four seeds of sequence selection.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: Accuracy should stay close to the reference at every bit-width and the 32-bit camera head should change little. If any bit-width falls outside the seed spread of the reference, the concern about rounding does not arise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Pose and Geometry Fidelity of Rotation-Smoothed Low-Bit VGGT
PROPOSAL: Insert orthogonal rotations before the attention and feed-forward projections of VGGT, fold them into the weights, and quantize to 4-bit weights and 6-bit activations with 48 calibration sequences from CO3Dv2 and ScanNet. The accuracy of the camera outputs and the point maps is the target, because downstream use depends on trajectories and geometry and not on internal statistics. Evaluate on RealEstate10K, 7-Scenes and TUM RGB-D sequences.
CONTROLS: Measure the area under the curve of relative pose accuracy, the absolute trajectory error and the point map error against the full-precision reference. Compare the rotated model with the unrotated one under the same ranges. Check the same metrics on a second dataset and repeat the calibration draw with five seeds.
COST: 450
PREDICTION: Rotation should keep pose and point map metrics close to the reference, with trajectory error rising only slightly. The method fails if these metrics degrade even when internal statistics look healthy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Statistics Fidelity of Rotation-Smoothed Low-Bit VGGT Features
PROPOSAL: Insert orthogonal rotations before the attention and feed-forward projections of VGGT, fold them into the weights, and quantize to 4-bit weights and 6-bit activations with 48 calibration sequences from CO3Dv2 and ScanNet. The match of internal activation distributions is the target, because heavy tails and channel variance drive the rounding loss in each layer. Evaluate on the same sequences across all blocks, layer by layer.
CONTROLS: Measure the mean squared error of block outputs, the cosine similarity of layer features and the kurtosis of activations against the full-precision reference. Compare the rotated model with the unrotated one under the same ranges. Check the same metrics on a second dataset and repeat the calibration draw with five seeds.
COST: 450
PREDICTION: Rotation should keep feature error and similarity close to the reference, with kurtosis dropping sharply. The method fails if these metrics degrade even when the rotation is applied everywhere.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Diversity-Based Versus Random Calibration Draws for VGGT
PROPOSAL: Build calibration sets of 24 sequences by greedy farthest-point selection in the embedding space of the pretrained vision backbone, using candidate sequences from CO3Dv2, ScanNet and a driving corpus. Quantize VGGT to 8-bit weights and 6-bit activations with ranges fitted on each set, and measure camera pose accuracy and point map error on held-out scenes from all three sources, with ten independent draws.
CONTROLS: Compare farthest-point sets with uniformly random sets drawn from the full pool, with sets taken from a single source, and with sets made of sequences whose activations have the largest ranges, using the same quantizer and the same count. Use the full-precision model as reference and repeat every draw with ten seeds.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Farthest-point sets should lower the spread across draws and raise worst-case pose accuracy relative to random sets. The claim is refuted if their results match those of random draws within the seed spread.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cluster-Local Versus Random Calibration Draws for VGGT
PROPOSAL: Assemble calibration sets of 24 sequences from consecutive entries inside a single embedding cluster of the pretrained vision backbone, taking candidates from CO3Dv2, ScanNet and a driving corpus. Fit 8-bit weight and 6-bit activation ranges for VGGT on each set, then score camera pose accuracy and point map error on held-out scenes belonging to that cluster, over ten independent draws.
CONTROLS: Set cluster-local sets against uniformly random sets drawn from that same cluster, against sets taken from the neighbouring cluster, and against sets made of sequences whose names sort first, using the same quantizer and the same count. Use the full-precision model as reference and repeat every draw with ten seeds.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Cluster-local sets should show a small spread across draws and similar pose accuracy to random sets from that cluster. The claim is refuted if their results differ from random draws beyond the seed spread.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Folding Special-Token Scaling Into Adjacent Weights of VGGT
PROPOSAL: Estimate per-channel scale factors on 32 calibration sequences from CO3Dv2 so that the camera token and the register tokens no longer stretch the activation range, then fold each factor and its inverse into the neighbouring normalisation and projection weights offline. The network stays identical in full precision and adds no operation at test time. Quantize activations to 6 bits and weights to 4 bits, and evaluate pose accuracy and point map error on RealEstate10K and 7-Scenes.
CONTROLS: Compare against the unscaled quantized model, against the full-precision model, against a language-model scaling recipe with a single global exponent, and against scaling fitted on image tokens only. Report the per-block activation range before and after folding, and repeat with four seeds of sequence selection.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: Folded scaling should shrink the activation range of special-token channels and restore most of the pose accuracy lost without it. The direction fails if range statistics improve but accuracy does not.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learned Rounding for the Weights of VGGT Linear Layers
PROPOSAL: Optimise the rounding direction of each weight in the aggregator of VGGT on 32 calibration sequences from CO3Dv2, using block-wise reconstruction of outputs and leaving activations in 16-bit. Weights go to 3 bits, grouped in blocks of 128 channels, and the compressed model is evaluated on RealEstate10K and 7-Scenes for pose accuracy and point map error, with storage size of the weights recorded for every setting.
CONTROLS: Compare against nearest-integer rounding of the weights, against the full-precision model, against a group size of 64 with the same bit-width, and against rounding learned on image tokens only. Report the weight reconstruction error per block before and after learning, and repeat with four seeds of sequence selection.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: Learned rounding should lower weight reconstruction error and restore most of the accuracy lost by nearest rounding at 3 bits. The direction fails if error drops but pose accuracy does not move.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Embedding-Coverage Selection of Calibration Sequences for VGGT
PROPOSAL: Embed every candidate sequence from CO3Dv2 and ScanNet with the pretrained vision backbone, cluster the embeddings into 24 groups, and take the sequence nearest each centre to form a calibration set, then fit 8-bit activation ranges for VGGT on it. Evaluate camera pose accuracy and point map error on held-out scenes, and compare ranges fitted on sets drawn in ten independent runs with different cluster initialisations.
CONTROLS: Compare the coverage-driven sets with uniformly sampled sequences of the same count, with sets of the most atypical sequences, and with the full-precision model as reference. Evaluate on the same held-out scenes in every case, and report the mean and spread of each metric over the ten runs.
COST: 250
PREDICTION: Coverage-driven sets should give accurate ranges and a smaller spread across runs than uniform samples. The direction fails if coverage-driven sets perform like uniform samples.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Image-Quality Ranking for Choosing Calibration Frames in VGGT
PROPOSAL: Score every candidate frame in CO3Dv2 and ScanNet by sharpness, exposure and absence of motion blur, keep the top-ranked frames to form calibration sequences of 12 frames each, and fit 8-bit activation ranges for VGGT on a set of 24 such sequences. Evaluate camera pose accuracy and point map error on held-out scenes, and compare ranges fitted on sets of the best frames chosen in ten independent runs with different thresholds.
CONTROLS: Compare the quality-ranked sets with uniformly sampled frames of the same count, with sets from the lowest-ranked frames, and with the full-precision model as reference. Evaluate on the same held-out scenes in every case, and report the mean and spread of each metric over the ten runs.
COST: 250
PREDICTION: Sets made of sharp, well-exposed frames should give accurate ranges and a small spread across runs. The direction fails if quality-ranked sets perform like uniform samples.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Integer Kernels and Measured Savings for Quantized VGGT
PROPOSAL: Implement packed 4-bit weight and 8-bit activation matrix-multiplication routines for the aggregator of VGGT and run the quantized model on a physical accelerator, processing sequences of 8, 16 and 32 frames from CO3Dv2. Record peak memory, frames per second and time spent in attention and feed-forward layers, and check relative rotation and translation accuracy on held-out RealEstate10K scenes in the same runs.
CONTROLS: Compare with the full-precision model and the half-precision model on identical sequences, with a simulated quantizer that keeps floating-point arithmetic to separate rounding effects from kernel effects, and with a kernel that unpacks weights before use. Repeat every timing twenty times and report the median and spread.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Packed kernels should cut weight memory by about three quarters and speed up long sequences by a visible factor. The direction fails if measured speed matches the half-precision model within the timing spread.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Operation Counts and Storage Estimates for Quantized VGGT
PROPOSAL: Implement a simulated 4-bit weight and 8-bit activation quantizer for the aggregator of VGGT that keeps floating-point arithmetic, and process sequences of 8, 16 and 32 frames from CO3Dv2. Record parameter memory, the number of integer operations per frame and the share of operations spent in attention and feed-forward layers, and check relative rotation and translation accuracy on held-out RealEstate10K scenes in the same runs.
CONTROLS: Compare with the full-precision model and the half-precision model on identical sequences, with a counting script that assumes ideal integer speed to separate storage effects from arithmetic effects, and with a variant that unpacks weights before use. Repeat every count twenty times and report the median and spread.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Counted operations should fall by a large factor and parameter memory by about three quarters. The direction fails if estimated savings match the half-precision model within the counting spread.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scene-Level Held-Out Evaluation of Quantized VGGT Ranges
PROPOSAL: Fit 8-bit activation ranges for VGGT on 48 frames sampled from 40 ScanNet sequences, and evaluate the quantized model on entirely different scenes: further indoor rooms, object-centric captures from CO3Dv2 and outdoor trajectories from KITTI. Report relative pose accuracy and point map error, together with the change of results as the visual gap between fitting scenes and evaluation scenes grows.
CONTROLS: Compare the ranges fitted on indoor sequences with ranges fitted on a mixed set of all three kinds, with ranges fitted on the evaluation scenes themselves, and with the full-precision model as reference. Use the same evaluation scenes in every case and repeat the sequence sampling with five seeds.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Ranges should transfer well to similar rooms but lose accuracy on object captures and outdoor trajectories. The direction fails if accuracy stays close to the reference everywhere.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Frame-Level Held-Out Evaluation of Quantized VGGT Ranges
PROPOSAL: Estimate 8-bit activation ranges for VGGT from 48 frames sampled across 40 ScanNet sequences, then test the quantized model on further frames cut from those very sequences, split off before estimation. Report relative pose accuracy and point map error, plus how results change as the temporal distance between fitting frames and test frames within a sequence grows.
CONTROLS: Set ranges from sampled frames against ranges from the first frames of each sequence, against ranges from every second frame, and against the full-precision model as reference. Use the same test frames in every case and repeat the frame sampling with five seeds.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Ranges should transfer well to nearby and distant frames of the same sequences, with accuracy close to the reference. The direction fails if accuracy drops as the gap between frames grows.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Joint 4-Bit Weight and Activation Quantization With Rotations in VGGT
PROPOSAL: Bring the weights and activations of the VGGT aggregator down to 4 bits, inserting orthogonal rotations before projections so that the heavy-tailed special-token channels spread out, with ranges fitted on 32 calibration sequences from CO3Dv2. Evaluate pose accuracy on RealEstate10K, point map error on 7-Scenes and peak memory on 32-frame sequences, comparing each result with the pretrained model.
CONTROLS: Compare the rotated 4-bit model with the unrotated 4-bit model, with the full-precision model, and with 8-bit activations paired with 4-bit weights. Keep the calibration sequences fixed and repeat their selection with four seeds, reporting the spread of each metric.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Rotations should keep 4-bit accuracy within a few points of the pretrained model and cut memory sharply. The direction fails if accuracy collapses despite the rotations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reduced Image Size and Frame Count to Cut VGGT Cost
PROPOSAL: Keep the weights and activations of the VGGT aggregator in full precision, but shrink the input image size from 518 to 224 pixels and cap each sequence at 8 frames, with ranges of the remaining tokens unchanged on 32 calibration sequences from CO3Dv2. Evaluate pose accuracy on RealEstate10K, point map error on 7-Scenes and peak memory on 32-frame sequences, comparing each result with the pretrained model.
CONTROLS: Compare the reduced-size input with the original input size, with the full-precision model at 8 frames, and with 16 frames at the reduced image size. Keep the calibration sequences fixed and repeat their selection with four seeds, reporting the spread of each metric.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Smaller inputs should keep pose accuracy within a few points of the pretrained model and cut memory sharply. The direction fails if accuracy collapses despite the reduced size.
